classical_check: Silent: the Kalsarpa pattern is not classical; the four-placement version is his teaching.

gist: Repeats that if Rahu and Ketu are in any other boxes there is no Kalsarpa.

hindi: कालसर्प बहुत बड़े-बड़े ऋषियों को मुनियों को बड़े-बड़े मिनिस्टर्स को रहा है
says: Claims that Kalsarpa has been present in the charts of great rishis, munis and powerful ministers, implying the yoga does not stop anyone from greatness.
ambiguity: 'रहा है' is short: it could mean 'has been present in their charts' or 'has troubled them'; the next sentence about the fear of it suggests the first.
classical_check: Not checkable: no classical text lists Kalsarpa charts of sages or ministers.

gist: Says the superstition about Kalsarpa has ruined the whole world.

hindi: अगर मान लो यहां पर साथ में मंगल है लेकिन मूव करके वो यहां आ गया है ऐसा भी होता है दो दो राशि बदल जाते हैं ग्रह
says: Says a planet that sits with the nodes on one side in the sign chart can move across to the other side in the bhava-chalit chart, and planets can even shift by two houses, which would break the one-sided pattern.
cells_derived_method: Whether a planet crosses a house border depends on its degree in the sign and on the lagna degree; planets near the first or last 10 degrees of a sign, and houses near the angles, are the likely movers. The house number of the node axis decides which side the mover lands on.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Ketu with Mars in the 7th in Aries, lagna Libra at about 5 degrees; Mars at 28 degrees Aries falls in the 8th house of an equal-division chalit chart (7th runs 20 Pisces to 20 Aries), so it leaves the 2-to-6 side and the pattern breaks.

Derived: Rahu with Mars in the 10th in Pisces, lagna Gemini at about 25 degrees; Mars at 2 degrees Pisces falls in the 9th of the chalit chart (10th runs 10 Pisces to 10 Aries), so it joins the 5-to-9 half and breaks a spread of the others in houses 11 to 3.

ambiguity: 'दो दो राशि बदल जाते हैं' could mean a planet shifts two houses, or that two planets change sign-house at once; which side Mars started from is only in his drawing.
classical_check: Bhava-chalit shifting is standard Parashari/Sripati practice, but a planet normally moves at most one house, so a shift of two is unusual; Kalsarpa itself is not classical.

gist: Quips that astrology is very complex and a person does not know where to bang his head.

hindi: ये तो कालसर भंग हो गया है लेकिन वह चलित निर्ण भाव केपी कुंडली में होगा यह कुंडली होती है सूक्ष्म गणित होता है
says: Says the breaking (bhang) of Kalsarpa is only visible in the finer house charts (chalit, nirayana-bhava style, KP), which need subtle calculation and are not the plain sign chart.
ambiguity: 'निर्ण भाव' is garbled; it may be 'nirayana bhava' or a Sripati/nirnaya house chart.
classical_check: Bhava chalit is a real classical house method; judging a yoga by it is accepted in practice, while Kalsarpa itself is not classical.

hindi: दिखने को मंगल यही है तो लगेगा सारे ग्रह तो यही है कालसर्प है ऐसा लगेगा कि कालसर्प है लेकिन कालसर्प होगा नहीं भंग हो गया है
says: Warns that the plain sign chart can show a false Kalsarpa: with every planet apparently on one side it looks real, but if one planet really sits across the line in the finer chart the yoga is broken and does not operate.
classical_check: Silent on Kalsarpa; the general idea that bhava placement can override sign placement is Parashari, though not stated for this yoga.

gist: Mocks people who stay stuck in the Kalsarpa worry and wail 'haye Kalsarpa' all their life.

hindi: एक बार कालसर्प का स्यापा मुका लो जाओ पूजा करके आओ काल हस्ती के मंदिर में और स्यापा सिर से निकाल दो
says: Remedy: do the Kalsarpa puja once at the Kalahasti (Srikalahasti) Rahu-Ketu temple so the anxiety about it is finished and removed from the mind.
ambiguity: 'काल हस्ती' is read as Srikalahasti in Andhra Pradesh.
classical_check: Srikalahasti is the popular Rahu-Ketu dosha temple, but classical texts do not prescribe it, since Kalsarpa itself is modern.

gist: Says that otherwise the head stays disturbed with 'my Kalsarpa' worry; a person ruins his own mind (some words garbled).

hindi: इसलिए कराओ स्यापा मुका होगा कुछ नहीं उससे लेकिन कराओ
says: Concedes that the Kalsarpa puja will change nothing in itself, or that Kalsarpa itself does nothing, yet advises doing it anyway so the matter is closed; the remedy is for peace of mind.
ambiguity: 'होगा कुछ नहीं उससे' can mean the puja has no real effect, or that nothing bad will come from the yoga; both fit the sentence.
classical_check: Silent; a puja done only as psychological closure is not a classical remedy concept.

hindi: एकावली योग तब होता है जब राहु और केतु दूसरी जगह मूव किए हुए हैं ... और बाकी ग्रह उसके एक साइड है उसे एकावली कहते हैं
says: Defines Ekavali yoga as the same one-sided planet pattern as Kalsarpa but with Rahu and Ketu on the other, non-kendra axes; he gives it a separate name.
cells_derived_method: Ekavali covers the four non-kendra axes (2-8, 3-9, 5-11, 6-12); the axis houses and signs only change the topic, since he says to ignore it anyway.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Rahu in the 6th in Capricorn with Ketu in the 12th in Cancer, lagna Leo; with all planets on one side he would call it Ekavali and say ignore it.
Derived: Rahu in the 3rd in Virgo with Ketu in the 9th in Pisces, lagna Cancer; a one-sided spread is Ekavali for him, though a popular Kalsarpa definition would still name it Kalsarpa.
Derived: Rahu in the 8th in Gemini with Ketu in the 2nd in Sagittarius, lagna Scorpio; same Ekavali label if all other planets sit in houses 9 to 1 or 3 to 7.

ambiguity: 'दूसरी जगह' (other places) is taken to mean every non-kendra axis; his drawing with several marked positions is not visible in the caption.
classical_check: This Rahu-Ketu meaning of Ekavali is not a standard classical yoga as far as I know; the name is used loosely in modern usage.

hindi: इसको टोटली इग्नोर करो इसका कोई लेनदेन नहीं है
says: Tells students to ignore Ekavali completely, saying it has no bearing on results.
classical_check: Silent: Ekavali in this sense is not classical, so ignoring it contradicts nothing.

hindi: जब आप ग्रह को पकड़ के सही उपाय कर लेते हो कुछ वास्तु के कुछ रत्नों के आपका जीवन भर के लिए मामला सेट हो गया
says: Claims that once the right planet is identified and the correct remedy is done, partly vastu and partly gemstones, the matter is settled for the whole life.
ambiguity: 'ग्रह को पकड़ के' is read as correctly diagnosing which planet is at fault.
classical_check: Classical texts list gems and donation per planet but promise no permanent one-time cure; the lifetime-settled claim is his.

hindi: रत्नों का स्यापा सिर्फ यह महंगे सस्ते उपाय करो घूमते रहो सारी जिंदगी एक बार सर्जरी कराओ स्यापा मुका
says: Contrasts endless trial of cheap and costly remedies all through life with doing one precise 'surgery' once, and says the single exact remedy ends the gem and remedy hassle.
ambiguity: The opening 'रत्नों का स्यापा सिर्फ यह' is clipped; the meaning is inferred from the rest of the sentence.
classical_check: Silent; a one-time precise remedy versus repeated remedies is his own advice.

gist: Says others hand out all kinds of things for money, money being the smallest thing; trails off with 'khair'.
Garbled interjection 'samay khela' and an audience reply 'haan ji hukam'.

hindi: किसी का कोई कसूर नहीं है बच्चे के कर्म है मां-बाप के कर्म है पूर्व जन्म पूर्व जन्म के हैं
says: Says that being born with all planets on one side of Rahu-Ketu is nobody's fault; it comes from the child's own karma and the parents' karma of past lives.
classical_check: The karma view matches the general Parashari idea that the chart reflects past deeds; Kalsarpa itself is not classical.

gist: Says the question of what karma causes such births would be a separate, beautiful class of its own.
Parents curse and complain, asking what deed of theirs made the child like this (words garbled).

hindi: कई ऐसे लोग आते हैं मां-बाप बच्चे की बीमारी की पत्री लाते हैं कि बीमार है मैं कहता हूं पहले अपनी लाओ
says: When parents bring a sick child's chart, he asks for the parents' own chart first, treating the child's trouble as something read through the parents' karma. He is not diagnosing any illness.
cells_derived_method: He names no house; the classical child points in the parents' chart are the 5th house, its lord and Jupiter as karaka, and the sign on the 5th changes which planet is read.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: 5th house in Scorpio, lagna Cancer; Mars as 5th lord and any tie of it with Saturn or Rahu is what a classical reader would check for sorrow through children.
Derived: 5th house in Pisces, lagna Scorpio; Jupiter is both 5th lord and karaka, so its strength is the main thing to check.

ambiguity: He gives no house or planet rule here; the 5th-house and Jupiter pointers are the classical default, not his words.
classical_check: Classical texts judge progeny from the parents' 5th house and Jupiter; reading the child's illness from the parents' chart is a common practice but not a defined rule.

hindi: तुम्हें इससे सुख लेना लिखा ही नहीं है उनकी कुंडली में सुख लेना ही नहीं लिखा बच्चे से वो बच्चा दुख ही देगा
says: Says some parents simply have no happiness from a child written in their own chart, and such a child will give only sorrow; a fatalistic claim with no house or planet named.
cells_derived_method: He names no placement; classical logic would look at the 5th house, its lord and Jupiter, and a heavily afflicted 5th with a weak karaka is the usual pattern for 'no joy from children'.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: 5th house in Capricorn, lagna Virgo; Saturn (own sign) in the 5th with Jupiter weak or afflicted is the classical delay or limitation signature, not something he stated.
Derived: 5th house in Leo, lagna Aries; the Sun as 5th lord pressed by Rahu or Saturn, with Jupiter weak, would be read as strain through children.

ambiguity: Whether 'sukh na likha' is meant for the 5th house or for the parents' whole karma is not stated.
classical_check: Classical texts do give afflicted-5th combinations for sorrow through children, but he cites none; the blanket 'will give only sorrow' is stronger than any text.

hindi: फिर वह बच्चा दान करना पड़ता है यह सब
says: Says that in such cases the child eventually has to be donated, that is given away; a harsh tradition claim given without any chart rule.
ambiguity: 'दान करना पड़ता है' may be literal or a symbolic ritual transfer of the child.
classical_check: Not in BPHS; symbolic giving or selling of a child exists in some regional remedies for birth afflictions, to my knowledge, but it is folk practice and not a classical rule.

gist: Host says 'yes sir' and reads the next question, which is about gemstones.
Question: someone read in a book that fasting, charity and mantra chanting are the only three remedies and that gemstone remedy is not a thing.

hindi: तो वसे हमने वो रेडी क् फस्टिंग दान बहुत नॉर्मल चीजें हैं
says: Replies that fasting and donation are very ordinary, basic remedies, setting up the point that gemstone remedy is the technical, higher-skill one.
ambiguity: The first half of the sentence is garbled ('वो रेडी क्'); the fasting and donation part is clear.
classical_check: Classical remedy lists include mantra, dana, vrata, puja and gems together; his ranking of them is his own.

hindi: जेम स्टोस इतना ज्यादा टेक्निकल है ये एक ऐसे सर्जन की तरह है जो सर्जन न्यूरो सर्जन है
says: Says gemstone prescription is highly technical, comparable to neurosurgery, so the outcome depends on the skill of the person prescribing.
classical_check: Silent; classical gem texts give grading and planet rules but not a skill-level claim like this.

gist: Robotic surgery analogy: robots now catch 10 nm nerves while brain nerves are said to be 4 nm and only humans can do it yet (figures look wrong).
Analogy continues: robots will manage it later, the human brain is that fine and powerful.
Neurosurgeons who operate for very long hours are specialists whose brain operations look like miracles (the '181 hours' is a caption error).

hindi: तो ऐसा कोई जेनन बंदा जिसको इस में भयंकर नॉलेज हो कि कितने कलर में नीला कितने कलर का पीरा
says: Says the gem prescriber must have deep knowledge of exact shades, such as which tone of blue or which tone of yellow; knowing only the stone type is not enough.
ambiguity: 'जेनन' is garbled and probably means a gem expert; 'पीरा' is read as 'पीला' (yellow).
classical_check: Classical gem texts do grade colour and quality, but no text ties the shade to the chart this finely.

hindi: पन्ना नाम का एक पत्थर होता जो 5000 का भी आता है और 5 लाख भी कौन सा कितना नीला पीला चाहिए हरा चाहिए जो यह जानता है वह काम करेगा
says: Uses emerald (panna) as the example: one stone type can cost 5,000 or 5 lakh, and only someone who knows exactly which shade the person needs will make it work.
cells_derived_method: Emerald is Mercury's gem; whether and how strongly it is used depends on Mercury's house and sign condition in the chart.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Mercury in the 1st in Virgo (exalted), lagna Virgo; Mercury rules lagna and 10th, so a good-grade emerald is the least risky case.
Derived: Mercury in the 8th in Pisces (debilitated), lagna Leo; a weak Mercury in a dusthana would call for a careful, conservative shade and grade.

ambiguity: He lists blue, yellow and green in one breath; emerald itself is green, so the colour list is loose. The price figures may be caption errors.
classical_check: Emerald for Mercury agrees with the standard planet-gem table; shade-by-chart matching is his teaching.

hindi: ऐसे कुछ पहन लोगे पुखराज उससे कुछ नहीं होगा तुक्के से हो गया हो गया साइड इफेक्ट मार गया तो मर गया
says: Warns that wearing a stone such as yellow sapphire (pukhraj) at random will do nothing or work only by luck, and if a bad side effect strikes the damage is severe. This is a warning about harm, not a medical or death prediction.
cells_derived_method: Whether Jupiter's stone is safe depends on what Jupiter rules and where it sits; classical practice cautions when Jupiter owns dusthanas or marak houses for the lagna.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Jupiter in the 8th in Sagittarius (own sign), lagna Taurus; Jupiter rules the 8th and 11th, so a classical reader would be cautious about yellow sapphire.
Derived: Jupiter in the 5th in Pisces (own sign), lagna Scorpio; Jupiter rules the 2nd and 5th and is karaka of the 5th, so the stone is usually seen as supportive.

ambiguity: 'मर गया' is colloquial for 'is ruined' and not necessarily literal death.
classical_check: Classical texts also warn against wearing a gem for an unfit planet, but none says it causes severe harm by chance; the strength of the claim is his.

hindi: यह कलर पहचानने की खोपड़ी जिसके पास है वह चीज काम करती है यह है टेक्निकल
says: Says the real working ingredient is the person's ability to recognise the right colour: whoever has that eye makes the gem work, and that is what he means by the remedy being technical.
classical_check: Silent; effectiveness resting on the prescriber's colour judgement is his own claim.

gist: Cobbler and tailor analogy: a skilled craftsman's work is exceptional; begins a doctor example that continues in the next line.
Doctor analogy: a doctor knows which combination to give with paracetamol, and the fee is for that knowledge, not the pill.
Mangeram anecdote: the man who knows where to hit the generator with a hammer is paid for his knowledge.

hindi: जेम स्टोन जो जानते नहीं उनके प जेम स्टोन अटैक भी मारते हैं
says: Says gemstones can actually strike back at people when they are given or used by those who do not know the science.
ambiguity: 'उनके प' is cut off: it can mean the stone hits wearers who are given it by the ignorant, or hits the ignorant themselves.
classical_check: Classical texts say a wrongly chosen gem gives adverse results; the idea of it 'attacking' is a stronger colloquial form.

hindi: इसलिए बहुत सीरियस है क्योंकि जेम स्टोन उठाएगा नहीं तो तबाह कर देगा बहुत पावरफुल होते हैं
says: Concludes that gem therapy is very serious because the stone is two-edged and powerful: it will either lift the person up or wreck them.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit with the classical caution that a gem for a functional malefic planet can backfire; the wording is stronger.

gist: Someone also asked about Pitambari; he says Pitambari deserves its own class.
Says this is his own study from this life and he has many such combinations (words partly garbled).

hindi: ये मूलाधार का कॉमिनेशन है हम इसके अंदर बृहस्पति शनि को कंबाइन करते हैं
says: Describes Pitambari as a combination stone linked to the Muladhara (root) chakra, made by combining Jupiter and Saturn in one stone.
ambiguity: The caption gives 'ये मूलाधार का कॉमिनेशन है' without saying why Muladhara; the identification of Pitambari with this combination is inferred from the sentence before.
classical_check: Classical texts list one stone per planet and no Jupiter-Saturn blend; the chakra-planet link varies by school.

hindi: हो सकता है आपको पुखराज सूट नहीं करता लेकिन पहनाना पड़ेगा तो पीतांबरी पहनाना पड़ता है नीलम सूट नहीं करेगा यह पता है लेकिन पहनाना ही पड़ेगा
says: Says that when the chart needs Jupiter's or Saturn's stone but the pure stone would not suit the person, he still prescribes it in a modified form, Pitambari in place of yellow sapphire and an altered blue sapphire.
cells_derived_method: The conflict arises when a planet is needed for strength yet owns unfriendly houses for that lagna; which stone is softened depends on those lordships.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Jupiter in the 12th in Pisces (own sign), lagna Aries; Jupiter rules the 9th and 12th, so a needed pukhraj may be softened to a blend.
Derived: Saturn in the 6th in Capricorn (own sign), lagna Leo; Saturn rules the 6th and 7th, so a needed blue sapphire may be diluted rather than worn pure.

ambiguity: Why the stone is 'needed' even when it does not suit is not explained here.
classical_check: Classical gem rules say do not wear a gem for a planet that does not suit you; prescribing it anyway in a blended form is his own practice.

hindi: क्योंकि नीलम चाहिए लेकिन नीलम का कॉमिनेशन तोड़ देते हैं हम उसमें वाइट मिक्सिंग करते हैं येलो मिक्सिंग करते हैं उसका कलर डाउन बहुत टेक्निकल है
says: Explains the method for an unsuitable blue sapphire: he breaks its pure combination and mixes in white and yellow to tone the colour down, which he calls very technical.
ambiguity: It is not clear whether the mixing is of the stone itself or of the colour of a combination stone.
classical_check: Not found in classical gem texts; blending white and yellow into a blue sapphire is his own technique.

hindi: वास्तु के स्पेशलिस्ट क्यों उठे हुए हैं कई वो जानते हैं लाल रंग कर दो कितना लाल बस जादू यही
says: Says vastu specialists succeed because they know exactly how much of a colour to apply, for example red and how much red, and that this precision of shade is the magic.
ambiguity: 'उठे हुए हैं' is probably 'टिके हुए हैं' (are established); he names red but no planet, though red is classically Mars.
classical_check: Vastu texts give colours by direction and deity but not graded intensity; the shade-precision claim is his own.

hindi: है उसी के पैसे लेते हैं वो कितना पीला कितना नीला उसी के पैसे लेते हैं वो पैसे ले लेते हैं हम ऊर्जा लेते हैं हम ज्यादा लालची हैं
says: Gem sellers charge according to how yellow or how blue a stone looks, that is, by colour grade. He says the astrologer takes the stone's energy instead of money, and jokes that this makes the astrologer the greedier one. The point is that a remedy stone should be judged by the energy it carries, not by its colour grade or price.
ambiguity: The sentence starts mid-thought. 'Yellow' and 'blue' most likely mean yellow sapphire (Jupiter) and blue sapphire (Saturn), but he names no planet here. 'Energy' (urja) is not defined.
classical_check: Silent. Classical gem texts judge stones by colour, clarity and flaws; the energy-versus-price framing is his own.

gist: Aside that children or the audience do not easily grasp this gem point, then 'never mind'; no astrology content.

hindi: सर किसी ने अभी आपने बताया था शनि और चंद्र का जो बताया था कि दबा हुआ मन रहता है तो उससे रिलेटेड पूछा है क्वेश्चन कि इसको कैसे ठीक करें
says: Read out from a viewer's question: earlier in the class he taught that a Saturn and Moon combination leaves a suppressed, held-down mind, and the viewer asks how to correct it. Recorded as his earlier rule as relayed by the viewer, not as a fresh statement.
cells_derived_method: Moon is the mind and Saturn is restraint, so the suppression is felt in the life areas of the house the pair occupies and the houses they rule. The pair in the 1st, 4th or 5th touches self, inner peace and thought directly; in the 8th or 12th it turns hidden and brooding. Sign matters: Moon exalted in Taurus softens it, while Saturn debilitated in Aries or Moon debilitated in Scorpio makes it heavier. This is derived, not said by him.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: lagna Aries, Moon (4th lord) with Saturn (10th and 11th lord) in the 1st house. Saturn is debilitated in Aries, so the restraint shows openly in personality: the person holds back feelings about career and ambitions.

Derived: lagna Aquarius, Moon (6th lord) with Saturn (1st and 12th lord) in the 4th house. Moon is exalted in Taurus, which softens the weight, so the pressure shows as a guarded home life and inner peace rather than open depression.
Derived: lagna Scorpio, Moon (9th lord) with Saturn (3rd and 4th lord) in the 8th house. The brooding is hidden: faith, luck and home peace feel locked in, and the person keeps worries private.

ambiguity: The viewer's wording only says 'Saturn and Moon'. It is unclear whether he means conjunction, mutual aspect or Moon in Saturn's sign. No house or sign is given.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit: Moon with Saturn is classically read as a heavy, inhibited or sorrowful mind, and popular practice calls it Vish yoga. Classical texts do not use the phrase 'suppressed mind'.

hindi: मम्मी के पांव दबाओ
says: His remedy for the Saturn and Moon suppressed mind just asked about: press your mother's feet, that is, do humble physical service to the mother.
ambiguity: He gives no day, duration or frequency, and does not say what to do if the mother is not alive. He then slips into a joke in the next sentence.
classical_check: Partly agrees: classical texts link the Moon to the mother and prescribe service of mother and elders for an afflicted Moon, and service of elders for Saturn. The feet-pressing form is a folk remedy not found in classical lists.

gist: He says 'press my feet' by mistake, apologises, jokes that humans make mistakes, and repeats 'my feet' while the audience laughs.
A viewer asks for the significance of white sapphire; he replies that these are very technical matters and moves on.

hindi: हमारे को इतना मरा सा शनि चाहिए होता है सफेद पुखराज में कि हम शुक्र की उत्तम के लिए उस पर काम करते हैं
says: In a white sapphire (white pukhraj) meant for Venus he wants only a very faint trace of Saturn present in the stone, so that the stone works to bring Venus to its best.
ambiguity: 'Mara sa' (dead-ish or faint) may be a mis-caption of 'halka sa' (light). Either way a small amount is meant. White pukhraj normally means white topaz or white sapphire; the viewer asked about 'white neelam'. Not said whether the Saturn trace is a colour tint or an energy blend.
classical_check: Silent. Classical lists give diamond for Venus, with white stones as substitutes in practice; a Saturn trace inside a Venus stone is not in them.

hindi: हृदय चक्र के लिए होता है जिसके न्यूरॉन्स की नर्व्स की प्रॉब्लम होती है जैसे हार्ट के अंदर ब्लॉकेजेस होती है तो उसके लिए अगर वो कुंडली अल करती है तो तो एक स्पेसिफिक मिक्सिंग का ब्लू कलर लेते हैं
says: This white sapphire with a Saturn trace is tied to the heart chakra. For nerve problems and blockage-type heart problems, provided the horoscope permits it, one takes a stone with a specific blend of blue. This is a health-related claim recorded only as his words; it is not a diagnosis and is not endorsed.
cells_derived_method: He says the chart must permit it but gives no rule. Derived method: before any such stone is considered, check that Venus and Saturn are functional benefics for the lagna (not lords of 6, 8 or 12, not marakas) and not afflicted. This is derived, not said by him.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: lagna Taurus, Venus in own sign in the 1st house, and Saturn is yogakaraka (9th and 10th lord). By this method a Venus stone carrying a Saturn trace is chart-supported.
Derived: lagna Aries, Venus in own sign in the 7th house. Venus rules the 2nd and 7th (both maraka houses) and Saturn rules the 10th and 11th, so the stone is not automatic and needs caution.

ambiguity: 'Kundali al karti hai' is garbled; probably 'allow karti hai' (if the chart permits). Link of the 'blue colour' to Saturn is inferred from the previous sentence, and 'heart chakra' (anahata) is named alongside a physical heart claim.
classical_check: Silent. Chakra-linked gem prescriptions and nerve or heart-blockage claims are modern practice, not classical Jyotish.

hindi: पत्थर चुनना मजाक नहीं है उस तरह का है हाईली के स्पेसिफिक वही वाला ही उसको काम करके क्लेरिटी देता है
says: Choosing a gemstone is not a casual matter. The stone has to be highly specific; only that exact kind of stone does the work and gives clarity to the problem it is meant for.
ambiguity: 'Clarity' may mean the gem's own clarity (transparency, flawlessness) or clarity of mind or result for the wearer; the caption does not settle it.
classical_check: Agrees broadly: classical and later gem texts insist on the right stone, weight and flawless quality chosen from the chart. The 'clarity' claim is his own wording.

hindi: कोलेस्ट्रॉल उड़ जाता है ब्लॉक नलिया खुल जाती है नश ठीक हो जाती है हड्डियों के जोड़ भर जाते हैं
says: Health claims for the stone just described: cholesterol vanishes, blocked tubes open, nerves are repaired and bone joints fill up. Recorded only as his stated claim. It is a medical claim, not validated, and must not be used as a prediction or advice.
ambiguity: 'Nash' is a caption slip for 'nas' (nerve or vein). 'Naliya' (tubes) probably means arteries or vessels. The planet link is inferred from the previous sentences, not repeated here.
classical_check: Silent. Classical Jyotish links planets to body parts and diseases but does not claim that gems clear cholesterol or blocked arteries; this is a modern remedy claim.

gist: Says gem selection is technical and that they will take it up sometime in a horoscope discussion or by looking at a live chart starting with a viewer's kundali.
Remarks that the charts of Ram and Krishna were taken up today, but the time ran into carrot halwa arriving; the caption is garbled and has no astrology content.
Banter that even the halwa is carrot halwa, that this adds to the mess, and that life is a difficult muddle.
Jokes that a loud remark is a way to wake those who are asleep; one person woke up, so he says it worked and moves to the next question.
Jokes that viewers should pray to the Mother for the questions to end, and that questions did end as soon as it was known the halwa was carrot halwa.
Closing of the class: thanks and namaste to everyone who joined, and gratitude to God that Jyotish could be discussed.
Opinion that this unique knowledge should be in the school syllabus, even at pass marks of 33, because childhood learning forms the roots.
Promotional claim that at any age one can 'become a rocket' with this knowledge and money will fall in the pocket because it is Vishnu karma and Lakshmi comes at the feet; not a chart rule.
Farewell: asks for blessings, says they meet again next week, thanks and namaste.
